posts.heading: September 17, 2026
posts.text: The day ended with 302 feeder visits and 21 species, marking a significant increase over the recent seven-day average of 169.9 visits. While the afternoon saw Carolina Wrens dominate the acoustic record, the final hours brought a shift back to the steady presence of Tufted Titmice and Northern Cardinals. The last visual record of the day was a Blue Jay at 19:33, just two minutes before sunset. This brief appearance closed out a day where Tufted Titmice accounted for 123 of the 302 total visits. As dusk settled, the chorus faded to the occasional call of a Northern Mockingbird and House Finch.

posts.heading: September 16, 2026
posts.text: The station closed out the day with 244 feeder visits and 23 species, figures that sit well above the seven-day average of 138 visits and 14 species. This high volume continues the trend established since the seed feeder was installed on September 13, replacing the unit that had been causing detection problems. Tufted Titmice remained the dominant visual presence, while Blue Jays led the acoustic record in the final hours.

posts.heading: September 15, 2026
posts.text:
The station’s activity on September 15 marked a sharp peak in volume, totaling 278 visits and 20 species observed, well above the previous week’s average of 98 visits. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees formed the core of the traffic, with Tufted Titmice alone accounting for 94 visits. This surge followed the installation of a new seed feeder on September 13, which replaced an older unit that had caused detection problems.

The acoustic record was equally robust, with Carolina Wrens leading at 126 detections and Northern Cardinals contributing 49. The shift to a new microphone on September 13, which has captured detections since then, underpins this clear auditory data. Regulars such as American Crows and Blue Jays were present daily, while first-time visual sightings at the station included a Black-capped Chickadee and a Common Gallinule, both species outside the regional norm for this week.

The day’s activity was sustained across all hours, from early morning visits by Tufted Titmice to evening calls by Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays.

posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text:
The station saw its busiest day in the past week, recording 244 visits against a seven-day average of 63.6. This spike follows a steady rise from 22 visits last Wednesday to 142 yesterday, marking the highest total of the period. The new seed feeder installed yesterday morning resolved detection issues, allowing for a clear count of high-traffic regulars like Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees.

Acoustic records show a dramatic increase in activity, with 129 Carolina Wren detections exceeding the previous weekly high. This aligns with the switch to the new audio source yesterday, which replaced the earlier microphone. While familiar species dominated the logs, a single Black-crowned Night Heron was heard late in the evening.

Visual records were led by Tufted Titmice with 96 confident sightings, followed closely by Carolina Chickadees at 69. Ruby-throated Hummingbirds were the earliest arrivals, first seen 13 minutes after sunrise and the last species recorded at sunset.
